display.purpose: The ABENOR wordmark only. Ships as server-rendered DOM text, is the LCP element, and hands its optical space to the WebGL particle mark once the canvas paints.

headline.purpose: Act headings. Always paired with a mono eyebrow on the same baseline and a 1px rule beneath.

title.purpose: Problem statements and step names. The largest thing that is a sentence rather than a label.

body-lead.purpose: Short sentences that earn display treatment. The hero paragraph and the single-sentence beats. Capped at 26ch.

body.purpose: All supporting prose, set in monospace. Capped at 46ch, never past 54ch.

label.purpose: Eyebrows, status bar, nav links, captions, attributions. The connective tissue of the page. Never wraps.

shadows.name: raised
shadows.purpose: The primary CTA and mockup frames. Three layers because a single soft shadow on a warm paper ground reads as blur rather than lift.

shadows.name: raised-lg
shadows.purpose: The largest floating object on a screen. At most one per viewport.

shadows.name: cta-glow
shadows.purpose: Primary button only. Tinted with the accent so the lift reads as heat, not as a generic drop shadow.

motion.name: ease-out-expo
motion.purpose: Default. Hover washes, reveals, anything entering or settling.

motion.name: ease-in-out-quart
motion.purpose: Symmetrical moves: curtain wipes, panel transitions that must feel deliberate at both ends.

motion.name: dur-press
motion.purpose: Pointer-down feedback. The one moment where perceptible delay reads as breakage rather than as motion.

motion.name: dur-ui
motion.purpose: Hover, colour, small state changes. Nothing a pointer triggers may exceed 300ms.

motion.name: dur-panel
motion.purpose: Disclosure and anything with height. The FAQ panel is the one sanctioned place to animate layout.

motion.name: dur-surface
motion.purpose: The paper/ink chrome handover. Deliberately slower than UI motion: it is a scene change, not a response.

narrative.overview:
Cooled metal is the ground and molten metal is the event. The surface is a warm, matte, slightly off-white that has been worked rather than printed on. Structure is cut into it with hairline rules, never floated on top of it with cards. The accent is heat: it appears where something is actually happening, and its rarity is what makes it read as heat rather than as branding.

The system is loud in scale and quiet in ornament. A wordmark can occupy the full measure of the viewport at 238px; the paragraph beneath it is 13px monospace with no decoration whatsoever. That gap is the entire aesthetic. Boldness is bought with size, weight, and the accent, never with gradients, glows, or containers.

This explicitly rejects two neighbors. It is not a corporate consultancy: nothing here is navy, nothing hedges, no surface exists to look expensive. It is not a generic Indian dev-shop site: no stock photography, no technology logo wall, no floating chat bubble, no grid of twelve identical service cards. Where those sites use decoration to imply competence, this one uses restraint plus one unmissable accent, and lets the interface itself be the evidence.
keyCharacteristics: Warm paper ground, near-black ink, a single molten orange that is spent sparingly and never diluted.
Sharp corners by default. Radius is 0 unless the element is depicting something physical (a phone, an app window).
1px rules carry all structure. Cards are a last resort, and never nest.
Monospace is the body voice, not an accent. Sans is reserved for scale.
Extreme scale contrast: a 238px display against 10.5px labels in the same viewport.
Heavy and confident components: real fills, thick hit areas, no timidity in the primary action.

rules.name: The Heat Rule
rules.body: Molten Pour is spent, not applied. If more than roughly 10% of a viewport is carrying the accent, something has been decorated rather than marked. The one exception is a deliberate inversion surface, where ink floods and the accent becomes ambient light.

rules.name: The Two-Orange Rule
rules.body: There are two oranges and they are not interchangeable. Molten Pour is for type above 18px and for non-text marks. Forged Deep is for everything a person has to read or click. Choosing by appearance rather than by size is how this system fails accessibility.

rules.name: The No-Grey-Guessing Rule
rules.body: Every neutral in this palette has a measured contrast ratio behind it. Never introduce a new grey by eye. Compute it against Cooled Steel first, or reuse Slag or Ash.

rules.name: The Two-Register Rule
rules.body: Bricolage shouts, Plex Mono explains. A sans paragraph of running body copy is wrong here, and a monospace headline is wrong here. The only sanctioned crossover is Body Lead, where a short sentence earns display treatment.

rules.name: The Wide-Gap Rule
rules.body: Adjacent type steps should differ by far more than 1.25x. This system routinely puts 238px next to 10.5px. If two elements are close in size, one of them is undecided; resolve it by pushing them apart, not by splitting the difference.

rules.name: The Measure Rule
rules.body: Monospace body copy is capped at 46ch. Uppercase mono labels never wrap; if a label does not fit, the label is cut at that breakpoint rather than allowed to run to a second line.

rules.name: The Drawn-Depth Rule
rules.body: If an element needs separating from what is around it, the first answer is a rule, the second is a tonal step of paper, and the third is nothing at all. A shadow is the fourth answer and requires a reason that survives the sentence 'this object is physically above the page.'

rules.name: The One-Float Rule
rules.body: No more than one shadowed element per viewport. Two competing floats collapse the whole flat system into a card layout.

dos: Do use Forged Deep (#C23A05) for any accent below 18px, and Molten Pour (#E8470A) only for display type and non-text marks.
Do separate content with a 1px Scribe Rule (#D4D2CC) or a tonal step of paper before reaching for a container.
Do set running body copy in IBM Plex Mono at 13px to 15px, capped at 46ch.
Do push adjacent type steps far apart. Extreme scale contrast is the system's main source of energy.
Do keep every corner square. Radius above 0 is reserved for frames depicting physical objects.
Do give the primary action a real fill, real padding (20px 40px), and the accent-tinted glow. The main ask should be the heaviest thing on the screen.
Do enforce a 44px minimum hit area with min-h-11.
Do label every mockup as illustrative, on the surface, in the interface. One invented number poisons the real ones.
Do ship a working reduced-motion path: canvas unmounted, DOM wordmark retained, reveals resolved to rest state.
donts: Don't build anything that could appear on a corporate consultancy site: navy and grey, stock gravitas, or a sentence that avoids committing to anything.
Don't reach for the generic Indian dev-shop vocabulary: stock photos of teams at laptops, a technology logo wall, a floating WhatsApp button, or a grid of twelve identical service cards.
Don't use border-left or border-right above 1px as a colored accent stripe. This was already removed once from the 200-hours callout; it is now a full border-y.
Don't use gradient text, background-clip: text, or any glow on type.
Don't add a second shadowed element to a viewport that already has one.
Don't introduce a new grey by eye. Every neutral here has a measured ratio.
Don't reveal copy on hover. It is invisible on touch.
Don't promote Quench Blue (#2B4FD0) beyond its single job in the heading hover split.
Don't write em dashes in interface copy. Commas, colons, semicolons, periods, parentheses.
Don't let a mono uppercase label wrap. Cut the content at that breakpoint instead.
